blocks.content: Temple architecture in ancient India was not merely a construction of worship places, but an expression of cosmic order and deep philosophical thought.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Nagara style is characterized by a beehive-shaped curvilinear tower (Shikhara) prominent in Northern India.
Dravida style temples feature high boundary walls, ornate gateway towers (Gopurams), and stepped pyramid towers (Vimana).
Vesara style developed under the Chalukyas and Hoysalas as a hybrid combining Nagara and Dravida elements.
The primary Char Dham circuit established by Adi Shankaracharya includes Badrinath, Dwarka, Puri, and Rameswaram.
Rock-cut temple architecture reached its zenith with the monolithic Kailash Temple at Ellora built by Rashtrakuta King Krishna I.
Key architectural contrast: Nagara style uses curvilinear Sikhara, whereas Dravida style features stepped pyramid Vimana and grand Gopurams.
Match dynasty patrons: Khajuraho Temples (Chandelas), Sun Temple at Konark (Eastern Ganga dynasty), Brihadisvara Temple (Rajaraja I Chola).
Differentiate between the All-India Char Dham (Badrinath, Dwarka, Puri, Rameswaram) and the Chota Char Dham of Uttarakhand (Yamunotri, Gangotri, Kedarnath, Badrinath).

cells: [EXAM TIP] Ganga Sagar Mela at Sagar Island (where Ganga meets Bay of Bengal) is one of India's largest pilgrimages — held every Makar Sankranti. ISKCON world headquarters is at Mayapur (Nadia), WB. Both are asked frequently.
